title: Topological Sort (Kahn's Algorithm)
summary: Order the vertices of a directed graph so every edge points forward. Vertices with no incoming edges go first; removing them frees the next ones. If some vertices are never freed, the graph has a cycle.

inputs.name: values
inputs.label: Directed edges
inputs.hint: Directed edges as pairs: from, to. For example 0, 1, 1, 2 means 0→1 and 1→2. Do not list both directions between the same two vertices.

inputs.name: vertices
inputs.label: Number of vertices
inputs.hint: From 1 to 8. Vertices are numbered 0 up to one less than this number.

anchors.label: Store the directed edges in a matrix
Count the incoming edges of every vertex
Queue every vertex with no incoming edges
Place it next in the order
Look at each vertex it points to
A cycle blocks the rest: no order
